public_rationale: In his December 11, 2024 post, Marcus said that problems like object permanence held true of all models, including the new Sora release that week. OpenAI's launch post, dated December 9, 2024, announced that release and said the deployed Sora 'often generates unrealistic physics' (e2). The same day, TechCrunch reported Marques Brownlee's hands-on review of the new Sora. Brownlee said it had the same flaws as other generative tools, namely object-permanence issues: objects passed in front of or behind each other in ways that made no sense, and disappeared and reappeared without reason (e1). The VideoPhy benchmark (version dated October 3, 2024) tested open and closed video models, including CogVideoX, Lumiere and Dream Machine. Its best model, CogVideoX-5B, made videos that followed both the caption and physical laws in 39.6% of cases (e3). Read plainly, the claim covers the leading models that were evaluated, not literally every model, and on that reading the evidence supports it. None of the cited items shows the problem had been solved by the post date.
limitations: 'All models' cannot be checked literally. The evidence covers only the models that were reviewed or benchmarked.
VideoPhy measures caption adherence and physical commonsense together, not object permanence specifically. The cited abstract does not list Sora among the models tested.
The Sora finding comes from one reviewer's hands-on testing, as reported by TechCrunch.
OpenAI's statement refers to unrealistic physics in general and does not name object permanence.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evaluations showing the December 2024 Sora, or leading video models in general, had largely solved object permanence by the post date.

evidence.explanation: OpenAI itself said the released Sora often generates unrealistic physics. This is consistent with continued physical-consistency problems.

evidence.excerpt: Our human evaluation reveals that the existing models severely lack the ability to generate videos adhering to the given text prompts, while also lack physical commonsense.
evidence.explanation: A 2024 benchmark of several open and closed video models found that even the best one followed physical laws in under 40% of cases. This supports the claim that such problems were widespread, though it measures physical commonsense broadly, not object permanence alone.
